text:
jamie: Hey — seeing a spike in 5xx from model-inference pods in eu-west-1 starting ~02:10 UTC. Error rate ~12%. Digging in, looks like outbound connect failures to S3 and internal feature-store, suspect NAT port exhaustion.

maria: Can you paste the logs and any netstat/ss output?

jamie: Logs snippet and `ss -s`:
```
[2026-03-18T02:11:23Z] ERROR fetch_model: connect() failed: I/O timeout (errno=104)
ss -s
TCP: total 50000 (estab 120) ...
TIME-WAIT: 38000
```

ryan: That `TIME-WAIT` count is wild. conntrack count is ~120k on the nodes I sampled. AWS NAT Gateway per ENI ephemeral ports look saturated — we're running into SNAT port limits and heavy short-lived connections. Are requests concentrated to a single NAT per AZ?

maria: Yes — routing table points most subnets at one NAT per AZ. Also noticed kube-proxy DNS churn + client retries after the DNS TTL drop. Sidecar-based metrics fetcher opens short TCPs per request which amplifies ports used.

alex: Did the svc-disc change that lowered DNS TTL land last night? I remember a PR that moved client-side TTL from 300->30s.

maria: That shipped in the 01:00 deploy (svc-disc-v2). Could definitely explain a burst of outbound connects after rollout.

jamie: Short-term mitigations I'm pushing:
- add an extra NAT Gateway in each impacted AZ (scale NAT count)
- enable gateway VPC endpoint for S3 to avoid NAT for model pulls
- throttle client concurrency / add retry backoff on the client side
- enable conntrack/tcp tuning on our proxies (temporary)

ryan: I'm spinning up extra NATs and updating the route tables now.

infra-bot: deploy:created nat-gw-eu-west-1a-2 (id nat-0abc1234), nat-gw-eu-west-1b-2 (id nat-0def5678). Route tables updated.

maria: After the extra NATs came up the 5xx dropped from ~12% -> ~1.2%. Nice. TIME_WAIT is still high though. We should patch node kernel tunables: `net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1`, lower `tcp_fin_timeout` for our proxy hosts, and ideally reduce short-lived connection patterns.

alex: Longer term: use connection multiplexing (eg. egress proxy or eBPF-based SNAT multiplexer), prefer VPC endpoints for AWS services, and revert the aggressive DNS TTL change for internal services. Also consider per-AZ NAT scaling rules tied to ephemeral-port-utilization metrics.

jamie: Action plan: 1) Roll canary to revert svc-disc TTL to 300 for internal SRV records 2) Patch sidecar to reuse keepalive/long connections where possible 3) Enable S3 VPC endpoints in prod 4) Infra to run a NAT capacity/cost review and add alerts 5) Create tracking ticket INF-5421.

ryan: Created INF-5421 and assigned to infra-team; labels: cost/egress, natgw, eng-inference.

maria: Also adding an alert: ephemeral_ports_available < 1000 per AZ (on node exporter + NAT metrics).

jamie: Thanks. I'll watch metrics for 30m and follow up if anything else flares. :thumbsup:
